fatal_errors: The proposed HCP-to-BCC element-ratio optimization does not reconstruct the specific intervention of adding equiatomic Re to sputtered NbMoTaW films.
It omits the central defect-sink mechanism involving grain refinement, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and suppression of grain-boundary He-bubble growth.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
The irradiation, temperature, dose, energy, microstructure, and processing conditions are not specified.
The baseline is not composition- and processing-matched, so the predicted improvement cannot be attributed cleanly to the intervention.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of improving refractory high-entropy alloys for mechanical and irradiation service, but otherwise has little agreement with the target. It replaces Re addition to nanocrystalline NbMoTaW films with a vague HCP/BCC compositional ratio and invokes dislocation properties rather than irradiation-defect sinks and He-bubble suppression. Its outcomes are generic and unquantified, and it does not predict reduced irradiation hardening or grain-boundary embrittlement relative to matched Re-free films. The proposed composition series could test a broad optimization claim, but it lacks defined irradiation exposures, thermal-stability metrics, matched controls, and direct defect measurements such as cross-sectional TEM of He bubbles. Without prior evidence or operational definitions of the optimized ratio and maintained stability, it is not a well-supported alternative.
